title: Rep. Carey introduces bill in U.S. House to expand low-income housing tax credit carrybacks
text:
Rep. Carey introduces bill in U.S. House to expand low-income housing tax credit carrybacks
The new bill authored by U.S. Rep. Mike Carey in the U.S. House aims to broaden tax relief for affordable housing through expanded carryback provisions, according to the U.S. Congress.
H.R.9012 was introduced on May 22, 2026 during the 2026 regular session of the 119th Congress. The following is our breakdown, based on the actual bill text, and may include interpretation to clarify its provisions.
In essence, this bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to permit a five-year carryback for the low-income housing tax credit. The modification aims to broaden the scope of carrybacks available under the existing tax law by including the low-income housing tax credit alongside other specified credits. This change is designed to provide tax relief for developers and investors in affordable housing by allowing them to apply unused tax credits to prior taxable years, potentially increasing their financial stability and encouraging investment in low-income housing projects. The amendments will take effect for taxable years starting after the enactment of the bill.
The bill was introduced by Rep. Mike Carey (Republican-OH-15th District) and co-sponsored by Rep. Jimmy Panetta (Democrat-OH-19th District).
Since the beginning of the current session, Rep. Carey has introduced another 20 bills.
Congressional bills can originate in either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate, except for revenue-related measures, which must begin in the House. After introduction, bills are assigned to committees for review, hearings, amendments and debate before they can advance to a vote in each chamber. If both chambers approve identical versions, the legislation is sent to the president, who may sign it into law or veto it. Congress operates in two-year terms, with each term numbered sequentially and divided into two annual sessions. The legislative process and official bill records are maintained by the U.S. Congress and published through Congress.gov.
Mike Carey is a Representative from Ohio, elected as a Republican to the One Hundred Seventeenth Congress by special election to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of United States Representative Steve Stivers. He has been reelected to the two succeeding Congresses and has served in various staff roles, including for Ohio state senator Merle Grace Kearns and United States Representative Robert William Ney of Ohio.
Carey graduated from East Clinton High School in 1989 and earned an A.S. from Marion Military Institute in 1991, followed by a B.A. from Ohio State University in 1993. He served in the United States Army Reserve from 1989 to 1999.
